title: Signature Average hash (aHash) — Reverse Image Matching
description: Signature original — aHash shrinks any image to 8x8 grayscale, then sets each bit by whether the pixel beats the mean. The 64-bit result is a fingerprint: resizes and recompression barely move it. Hamming distance between fingerprints ranks near-duplicates in microseconds. title: Signature Perceptual hash (pHash) — Reverse Image Matching
description: Signature original — pHash applies a discrete cosine transform to the shrunken grayscale image and keeps the low-frequency coefficients. Low frequencies encode structure while ignoring fine noise, making pHash sturdier than aHash under edits. It is the workhorse hash for finding copies across re-encodes and resizes. title: Signature Difference hash (dHash) — Reverse Image Matching
description: Signature original — dHash compares each pixel to its right neighbor instead of the global mean, encoding gradients. Gradient bits survive brightness and contrast shifts that can flip aHash bits. dHash is often the best cheap hash for photographic near-duplicates. title: Signature Hamming distance ranking — Reverse Image Matching
description: Signature original — Two 64-bit hashes compare by Hamming distance: the count of differing bit positions. Distance 0-5 means near-certain duplicates; 6-10 means likely variants; beyond that, unrelated. Threshold choice trades recall of edited copies against precision.
